title: Thoryn provisioning file (.thoryn/provision.yaml)
description: SSO-3088 (epic SSO-3087) — the DESIRED STATE of a repository's Thoryn resources, converged idempotently by `thoryn provision plan | apply | destroy`. Resources, not steps: each has a stable `name` the CLI uses as its converge key. The `kind` values form a CLOSED allowlist mapping only to supported product APIs (the product-boundary rule made structural). Secrets NEVER enter this file: a key that carries a secret value is rejected; name the ENV VAR that carries it instead (`passwordEnv`, `smtpPasswordEnv`, `clientSecretEnv`).

kind.description: CLOSED allowlist of resource kinds, each mapping to one supported product API. `emailProvider`, `loginTheme`, `loginFlow` and `loginMethods` are singletons per environment (no `name` needed). `loginMethods` (SSO-3100) is the sign-in METHOD allow-list the hosted login offers (`PUT /api/v1/login-methods`; `destroy` resets it to the default via `DELETE`). `user` exists so a scenario can declare its test account; a customer's real users self-register.

name.description: Stable converge key (unique per kind within the file). Required for every non-singleton kind.

environment.description: The environment this resource lives in: the `name` of an `environment` resource in this file, or the slug of an environment that already exists. Omitted ⇒ the workspace's production plane. Not allowed on an `environment` resource.

spec.description: Kind-specific desired state, forwarded to the product API. Property names ending in password / secret / token are REJECTED — use `<key>Env` naming the env var that carries the value.

slug.description: A slug, or a `{{env.NAME}}` placeholder resolved from the environment at apply time (a per-run sandbox in CI).

methods.description: The FULL sign-in method allow-list, in display order (e.g. password, magic_link, magic_code, passkey, totp, sms); the server rejects an unknown token. Converged as a SET (order-insensitive).
